text:
Summary: Unbiased detection of protein–protein and protein–RNA interactions within ribonucleoprotein complexes
are enabled through crosslinking followed by mass spectrometry. Yet, different methods detect different types
of molecular interactions and therefore require the usage of different software packages with limited compatibility.
We present crisscrosslinkeR, an R package that maps both protein–protein and protein–RNA interactions detected
by different types of approaches for crosslinking with mass spectrometry. crisscrosslinkeR produces output
ﬁles that are compatible with visualization using popular software packages for the generation of publication-quality
ﬁgures.
Availability and implementation: crisscrosslinkeR is a free and open-source package, available through GitHub:
github.com/egmg726/crisscrosslinker.
Contact: chen.davidovich@monash.edu
Supplementary information: Supplementary data are available at Bioinformatics online.
1 Introduction
The function of ribonucleoproteins (RNPs) is dependent on protein–
protein and protein–RNA interactions. Chemical crosslinking with
mass spectrometry [XL-MS ; Fig. 1, top right] is
used for mapping protein–protein interactions. On the other hand,
the detection of RNA-linked peptides by mass spectrometry (MS) is
challenging, given complex MS signals of low intensity . This challenge is met by the RBDmap method: allowing to detect protein–RNA interactions using UV crosslinking followed by tandem proteolysis, using LysC or ArgC followed by
trypsin, combined with MS (Fig. 1, top left). Software packages are available for
initial processing of XL-MS data [e.g. pLink ] or
RBDmap data [e.g. MaxQuant ]. However, in
an RBDmap experiment, the MS-identified peptides are adjacent to
the RNA-linked peptides . Therefore,
downstream bioinformatic analysis reveals the RNA-linked peptides, given the protein sequence and the proteases used in the assay.
Hence, custom pipelines are needed to combine, compare or reduce
datasets obtained from different experiments, treatments and replicates, especially if RBDmap is complemented by XL-MS. Such custom analysis has remained a bottleneck for the study of RNP
complexes when both protein–protein and protein–RNA interactions are of interest.
Herein, we describe crisscrosslinkeR, an R package aimed to
identify molecular interactions detected from both types of XL-MS
experiments—XL-MS and RBDmap—and to map both protein–
protein
and
protein–RNA
interactions,
respectively.

and Degiacomi et al. 2017)]. crisscrosslinkeR was designed to fill
the gap between the primary analysis of MS data to the interpretation and visualization of the results either simultaneously for both
protein–RNA interactions and protein–protein interactions, or independently for any of them. To our knowledge, it is the first tool
that streamlines RBDmap data analysis and the first package dedicated for mapping both RBDmap and XL-MS data.
2 Implementation
Primary MS data analysis is performed by pLink ,
MaxQuant and Andromeda , which identify tryptic peptides from raw MS files (.raw)
(Fig. 1, middle). In the context of the MS data analysis pipeline,
crisscrosslinkeR is placed downstream of these software and utilizes
R packages and APIs for protein data bank (PDB) file reading and
the RCSB PDB mapping.
3 Features
Data reduction is done across multiple samples, allowing to merge
replicates or accept data points based on user-defined conditions
(e.g. only if the same crosslinked peptide appeared in n replicates).
Filtration is based on significance scores that were assigned during
the primary data analysis. crisscrosslinkeR is designed to handle an
unlimited number of XL-MS and RBDmap datasets simultaneously
for a direct comparison or data reduction, based on user preference.
There are currently no tools to visualize RBDmap data over
sequences [two-dimensional (2D) visualization] or structures (3D
visualization) of protein complexes, though these forms of visualization are popular and supported in case of XL-MS. crisscrosslinkeR
illustrate replicates or different experimental treatments for 2D representation of RBDmap data. For 2D visualization of XL-MS and,
optionally, RBDmap data, crisscrosslinkeR exports files compatible
with the user-friendly server xiView (Fig. 1,
bottom right). For 3D visualization of RBDmap and XL-MS data,
crisscrosslinkeR uses the RCSB PDB mapping API to identify the
most suitable 3D structure(s) in the PDB, aligns it to the sequence of
the protein used during the experiment and then uses the selected
structure for 3D visualization of either RBDmap or XL-MS data
(Fig. 1, bottom left). Specifically, crisscrosslinkeR generates a
Python script to launch PyMOL —a popular
and stable suite for molecular imaging—to generate publicationquality figures or for structural analysis. crisscrosslinkeR can be
used to hide or present color-coded crosslinking sites, including
based on the score applied by the primary software that detected
them [MaxQuant or pLink ], the number of times linked peptides was detected across
multiple replicates and differential crosslinked sites and, when applicable, the Euclidean crosslinking distances; all these are visualized
with large flexibility for user-defined color selection.
Collectively, crisscrosslinkeR is a versatile pipeline that streamlines the workflow, starting from multiple raw data files down to
publication-quality figures.
4 Conclusion
crisscrosslinkeR provides users with the ability to analyze and visualize data obtained from both RBDmap and XL-MS experiments
including
an
unlimited
number
of
replicates
and
treatments.
crisscrosslinkeR allows the user to combine replicates, or to search
for common crosslinking events among replicates or different treatments, in order to discover biological cues in a complex dataset.
These functionalities are complemented by 2D and 3D visualization,
tailored for subsequent communication of the results. The current
version of crisscrosslinker does not support solvent-accessible distances. These can be obtained using other software packages as Xwalk
 Jwalk and DynamXL
. To our knowledge, crisscrosslinkeR is the
first available package that streamlines XL-MS data analysis for the
discovery of both protein–protein and protein–RNA interactions
within the same macromolecular RNP complex or biological system.
